units.la: Can. I. Ugri Hunnis in Pannoniâ successerunt.
units.tr: Canon I. The Ugrians succeeded the Huns in Pannonia.

units.la: Facta qvidem fuit secunda Hun-norum in Pannoniam irruptio A. C. 744, qvo sub VII. Ducibus exercitu 200000 militum in Pannonias ve-nerunt: contra qvos Carolus M. & alii Imperatores Francorum magna bella gesserunt; sed stabile Imperium fundare non potuerunt.
units.tr: Indeed, the second invasion of the Huns into Pannonia took place in the year 744 AD, when they came into the Pannonias under seven leaders with an army of 200,000 soldiers. Against them Charlemagne and other emperors of the Franks waged great wars, but they were unable to establish a lasting empire.

units.la: Successerunt igitur Ugri seu Juhri circa A. C. 900, qui ingenti multitudine ex remotissima Scythia, atq; ab ultimo glaciali Oceano, adventantes hodiernum Imperium Ungarorum condiderunt. Nam qvos nunc vocamus Ungaros, non ab antiquis illis Hunnis, sed a recentioribus Ugris originem trahunt.
units.tr: The Ugrians, or Juhri, therefore succeeded around the year 900 AD. Coming in vast multitudes from the most remote Scythia and from the farthest icy ocean, they founded the present Hungarian empire. For those whom we now call Hungarians trace their origin not from those ancient Huns, but from the more recent Ugrians.
The Hungarians accept the Christian faith.

units.la: Ab his Ugris Germania ineffabiles calamitates sensit, cum eam irrumpentes obvia omnia sacra & profana prosternerent, & usq; ad Germaniam inferiorem omnia exscinderent sub regibus Taxon & Caizà & aliis, qvorum qvinq; simul suspendit Otto I Imperator Ratisponæ. Ex-
units.tr: By these Ugrians Germany suffered unspeakable calamities, for, breaking in, they overthrew everything in their path, sacred and profane, and laid waste everything as far as Lower Germany, under the kings Taxo and Caiza and others, five of whom Otto I, Emperor, had hanged at once at Regensburg. Ex-

units.la: Hæc Barbaries duravit usq; dum Ugri ad Fidem Christianam conver-terentur: id quod factum A C. 997 quō S. Stephanus religionem suscepit, cujus posteri varia fortunâ re-gnarunt.
units.tr: This barbarity lasted until the Ugrians were converted to the Christian faith. That happened in the year 997 AD, when St. Stephen received the religion, and his descendants afterwards reigned with varying fortune.

units.la: Anno 1242 Tartari Duce Ba-thi Hungariam invaserunt, & uni-versum regnum caedibus & incendio ita devastarunt, ut vix in omni histo-ria similis calamitas occurrat.
units.tr: In the year 1242 the Tartars, under their leader Batu, invaded Hungary and so devastated the whole kingdom with slaughter and fire that a similar calamity can scarcely be found in all of history.

units.la: Hungaria exteros Reges habere cæpit. Explicatio.
units.tr: Hungary began to have foreign kings. Explanation.

units.la: Primò ex Bohemis, postea ex Ba-varis, tertiò ex Andegavensibus, quar-tòtò ex Lützelburgicis, qvintò ex Hungaris, sextò ex Polonis, septimò ex Austriacis, penes qvos hodieq; Imperium manet.
units.tr: First from the Bohemians, afterwards from the Bavarians, thirdly from the Angevins, fourthly from the Luxemburgers, fifthly from the Hungarians, sixthly from the Poles, and seventhly from the Austrians, in whose hands the empire remains even today.

units.la: Primus Transylvaniæ Princeps fuit Stephanus Bathorius, postea Poloniæ Rex. - Deinde Principatus pervenit ad Bethlehemum Gaborem; ab hoc ad Georgium Ragotzi, cujus filius Georgius Ragotzi II, deinceps Principatum obtinuit; in cujus locum Turcarum Imperator A. C. 1657. Achatium Barckzai, & eo interemto Michaelem Apafi, posuit, qvi adhuc hodiè Turcici Imperatoris protectione gubernat.
units.tr: The first Prince of Transylvania was Stephen Báthory, afterwards King of Poland. Then the principality passed to Bethlen Gábor; from him to György Rákóczi, whose son György Rákóczi II next held the principality. In his place the Emperor of the Turks, in the year of Christ 1657, set up Achatius Barcsai, and when he had been killed, Michael Apafi, who still governs today under the protection of the Turkish Emperor.

units.la: Periodus I. Can. I. Turci Persia potiti.
units.tr: Period I. Canon I. The Turks gain possession of Persia.

units.la: Turciæ gens pastoritia circa A.C. 1000. in Persiam migrarunt, ibiqve A.C. 1038 regem creârunt Togrul-beck, quem Historici Græci ac Latini corrupte vocant Tangrolipicem.
units.tr: The pastoral people of the Turks migrated into Persia around the year 1000 after Christ, and there in 1038 they made king Togrul-beck, whom Greek and Latin historians corruptly call Tangrolipix.
The kingdom of the Turks is divided into Eastern and Western.

units.la: Occidentale complectebatur Asiam minorem, illudq; destruxit Godefridus Bullioneus A.C. 1098, cum terram Sanctam sive Hierosolymam recuperaret. Orientale sive Persi-cum destruxére Tartari.
units.tr: The Western kingdom comprised Asia Minor, and it was destroyed by Godfrey of Bouillon in 1098, when he was recovering the Holy Land, that is, Jerusalem. The Eastern or Persian kingdom was destroyed by the Tartars.

units.la: Turcæ denuò in Asia Mi-nore regnarunt.
units.tr: The Turks again ruled in Asia Minor.

units.la: Cùm tempestas ista Tartarica i-terum dissipata fuisset, Turcæ colle-cti denuò in Asia Minore potestatem suam instaurarunt A. C. 1200[?].
units.tr: When that Tartar storm had once more been scattered, the Turks, gathered together again in Asia Minor, restored their power in the year of Christ 1200[?].
The Turks erected a very vast empire.

units.la: Conditor ejus fuit Osman, unde etiam hodierna familia Imperatorum Turcicorum vocatur Osmanni-dorum, ipsorumq; Sedes Porta Osman-nica. Hic Osman A. C. 1300. fa-ctus Rex Turcarum brevi tempore maximum Imperium posteris suis reliqvit, ita, ut tertius ab illo Morad sive Amurad in ipsam Europam pe-netranetraret, adjutus avaritiâ Genuen-sium mercatorum, qui singulas Turcas pro singulis aureis nummis unâ nocte in Europam navibus suis transportarunt.
units.tr: Its founder was Osman, from whom the present imperial family of the Turks is also called Osmanidae, and their seat is the Ottoman Porte. This Osman, made king of the Turks in A.D. 1300, in a short time left a very great empire to his descendants, so that Murad, or Amurad, the third from him, penetrated into Europe itself, aided by the greed of Genoese merchants, who for a single gold coin per Turk transported the Turks into Europe in their ships in a single night.

units.la: Timur, vulgò Tamerlanes, poten-tissimus Tartarorum Imperator cir-ca A.C. 1399. ingenti prælio Bajaze-tham Imperatorem Turcarum supe-ravit, & vivum cavea ferrea inclusit, ac per Asiam spectaculo circumdu-xit.
units.tr: Timur, commonly called Tamerlane, the most powerful emperor of the Tartars, about A.D. 1399 defeated Bajazeth, emperor of the Turks, in a great battle, shut him up alive in an iron cage, and led him about Asia as a spectacle.
The Turks gain the Eastern Empire.

units.la: Quanquam Turcarum poten-tia dissipata & fracta penitus à Ta-merlane videretur, mox tamen illô discedente Turcæ recollecti Impe-rium amplissimum instaurarunt; ita quidem, ut A. C. 1453. die 29. Maij Constantinopolis à Mahumete II. Imperatore Turcarum expugnaretur, & occisò Constantino XV. Palæologo, Imperatore Orientis, quicquid ex Romanâ potentiâ superat ad Turcas concederet. Ab eò tempore Turcarum Imperatores Constanti-nopoli dominati sunt, ac vastissimam Monarchiam condiderunt.
units.tr: Although the power of the Turks seemed utterly scattered and broken by Tamerlane, nevertheless, once he had withdrawn, the Turks rallied and restored a very wide empire; so much so that on 29 May A.D. 1453 Constantinople was taken by Mahomet II, emperor of the Turks, and with Constantine XV Palaeologus, emperor of the East, killed, whatever remained of Roman power passed to the Turks. From that time the emperors of the Turks have ruled at Constantinople and founded a very vast monarchy.
They overthrew the Circassian Mamelukes in Egypt.

units.la: A. C. 1517 Selimus Turcarum Imperator Thomambajum, ultimum Ægypti Suldanum, superavit, & captum d. 4 Aprilis miserabiliter in portâ Urbis Alcahira unco suspen-dit.
units.tr: In A.D. 1517 Selim, emperor of the Turks, defeated Thomanbay, the last sultan of Egypt, and on 4 April, once captured, hanged him wretchedly on a hook at the gate of the city of Cairo.

units.la: Causa fuit dissidium Hungarorum in novo Rege creando; cum A. C. 1526 Ludovicus II. ad oppidum Mohatium à Solymanno Turcarum Imperatore occisus fuisset. Unde quidam Hungarorum elegerunt Ferdinandum Austriae Archiducem, fratrem Caroli V, alii Johannem Zepusium, Praefectum Transylvaniae; qui, cum viribus esset inferior, Turcas auxilio evocavit, qui ea occasione maximam partem Hungarorum oc-cuparunt.
units.tr: The cause was the discord of the Hungarians in creating a new king, since in A.D. 1526 Louis II had been killed by Suleiman, emperor of the Turks, at the town of Mohács. Hence some of the Hungarians chose Ferdinand, archduke of Austria, brother of Charles V, others John Zápolya, prefect of Transylvania; who, being weaker in forces, summoned the Turks to help him, and they on that occasion occupied the greater part of Hungary.

units.la: Initium hujus inclinationis fa-ctum A. C. 1622. die 12. Maij, quâ Turcæ Imperatorem suum Ofman-num II, juvenem improvidum & infelicem, publicè, velut vile aliquod mancipium, strangularunt. Qvam tyrannidem A C 1648. repetierunt, pari licentia strangulato Imperatore suo Ibrahimo sive Abrahamo. Unde omnis Imperii Turcici potestas penes Janitzaro[?] sive Milites Praetorianos hodie sita est: ex quo langvor iste, ut per tot annos Cretam sive Candiam, Insulam Maris Mediterranei, Venetis eripere non potuerint. Hodie Turcis praeest Mahumetes IV.
units.tr: The beginning of this decline was made in A.D. 1622, on 12 May, when the Turks publicly strangled their emperor Osman II, a young man lacking foresight and unlucky, as if he were some worthless slave. They repeated this tyranny in A.D. 1648, with their emperor Ibrahim, or Abraham, strangled with the same licence. Hence all the power of the Turkish empire today lies with the Janissaries[?], or praetorian soldiers; from this came that weakness by which, for so many years, they have not been able to wrest Crete, or Candia, an island of the Mediterranean Sea, from the Venetians. Today Mehmed IV presides over the Turks.
The Tartars became masters of all Scythia.

units.la: Circa A.C. 1200 quidam Faber ferrarius, vel, ut alii volunt, Bubulcus, Scythis ad arma concitatis, & debellato Iohanne, Imperatore Nestoriano, amplissimum circa Sinam DImImperium constituit & Schingvi{s} Khan, i e. Rex Regum appellatus fuit. A quo tempore cuniversa Scythia Tartaria, Scythæ Tartari, sive, ut vulgo loquuntur, Tatari vocati fuerunt. Cujus nominis occasio inde fluxit, quod in illa expeditione Schingvis Khanica Tartari, qui fuerunt tribus sive Horda Scytharum, semper præmitterentur, adeoque, sparsa adventus eorum fama, cum populus passim inclamaret Tartaros advenire, nomen illud paulatim universo exercitui, mox toti genti, fuit impositum; ut quicunque obedirent Schingvi Khano, sive Imperatori Schytarum, Tartari dicerentur.
units.tr: Around the year 1200, a certain blacksmith, or, as others would have it, a herdsman, roused the Scythians to arms, defeated John, the Nestorian emperor, and established a vast empire around Sina. He was called Genghis Khan, that is, King of Kings. From that time the whole of Scythia was called Tartary, and the Scythian Tartars, or, as the common people say, the Tatars. The origin of this name was that in Genghis Khan's campaign the Tartars, who were a tribe or horde of the Scythians, always went ahead. So, when the news of their coming spread and the people everywhere cried out that the Tartars were coming, the name gradually passed to the whole army and soon to the whole nation. Thus everyone who obeyed Genghis Khan, that is, the emperor of the Scythians, came to be called a Tartar.

units.la: Cap. 2. Imperium Tartaricum divisum fuit in varia regna.
units.tr: Chap. 2. The Tartar empire was divided into various kingdoms.

units.la: Schingvis Khan paulo ante obitum suum inter filios suos universum... sum orbem debellandum divisit.
units.tr: Shortly before his death, Genghis Khan divided the whole world... to be conquered among his sons.

units.la: Qvatuor igitur exercitus Tartaro-rum versus omnes mundi plagas e-ruperunt, unus in Orientem atq; Si-nam; alter in Indiam; tertius in Per-siam; qvartus in ipsam Europam.
units.tr: Four Tartar armies therefore broke out toward all quarters of the world: one toward the East and China; another into India; a third into Persia; and a fourth into Europe itself.

units.la: Exercitus igitur Tartarorum Oc-cidentalium sub Duce Batku universa Russiam, Hungariam, Austriam, Poloniam & Silesiam vastavit, ac maxi-mô præliô Henricum Ducem Sile-siæ superavit. Hi Tartari vastissimum regnum condidere, quod vocabatur Desthense, i.e. Tartaria deserta; cu-jus Regibus tota Russia parebat. Alio nomine dicebatur Zavothense, quod trans Volgam, ad mare Caspium, situm erat. Hoc regnum destruxit circa A.C. 14co[?] Tamerlanes: ex cuius ruinis emerserunt regna Ca-san, Astracan, &c, quod hodieque famosissimum est, Crimense sive Præ-copense. Imperium constituit & Schingvi Khan, i e. Rex Regum appellatus fuit. A quo tempore universa Scythia Tartaria; Scythæ Tartari, sive, ut vulgo loquuntur, Tatari vocati fuerunt. Cujus nominis occasio inde fluxit, quod in illa expeditione Schingvis Khanica Tartari, qui fuerunt tribus sive Horda Scytharum, semper præmitterentur, adeoque sparsa adventus eorum fama, cum populus passim inclamaret Tartaros advenitare[?], nomen illud paulatim universo exercitui, mox toti genti, fuit impositū; ut quicunque obedirent Schingvi Khano, sive Imperatori Schytarum, Tartari dicerentur.
units.tr: The army of the Western Tartars under the leader Batu laid waste Russia, Hungary, Austria, Poland and Silesia, and in a very great battle defeated Duke Henry of Silesia. These Tartars founded a very vast kingdom, which was called Desthense, that is, Desert Tartary; all of Russia obeyed its kings. It was also called by another name, Zavothense, and lay across the Volga, toward the Caspian Sea. Around the year 1400 Tamerlane destroyed this kingdom. From its ruins arose the kingdoms of Kazan, Astrakhan, etc., and the kingdom of Crimea, or Perekop, which is still very famous today. Genghis Khan... was called King of Kings. From that time the whole of Scythia was called Tartary, and the Scythian Tartars, or, as the common people say, Tatars. The origin of this name was that in Genghis Khan's campaign the Tartars, who were a tribe or horde of the Scythians, always went ahead. So, when the news of their coming spread and the people everywhere cried out that the Tartars were coming, the name gradually passed to the whole army and soon to the whole nation; thus everyone who obeyed Genghis Khan, that is, the emperor of the Scythians, came to be called a Tartar.

units.la: Imperium Tartaricum divisum fuit in varia regna.
units.tr: The Tartar empire was divided into various kingdoms.

units.la: Schingvis Khan paulo ante obitum suum inter filios suos univer-sum sum[?] orbem debellandum divisit. Quatuor igitur exercitus Tartaro-rum versus omnes mundi plagas e-ruperunt, unus in Orientem atq; Sinam; alter in Indiam; tertius in Persiam; quartus in ipsam Europam.
units.tr: Shortly before his death, Genghis Khan divided the whole world... to be conquered among his sons. Four Tartar armies therefore broke out toward all quarters of the world: one toward the East and China; another into India; a third into Persia; and a fourth into Europe itself.

units.la: Exercitus igitur Tartarorum Occidentalium sub Due Bathu universa Russiam, Hungariam, Austriam, Poloniam & Silesiam vastavit, ac maximo prælio Henricum Ducem Silesiæ superavit. Hi Tartari vastissimum regnum condidere, quod vocabatur Disthense[?], i.e. Tartaria deserta; cujus Regibus tota Russia parebat. Alio nomine dicebatur Zavothense, quod trans Volgam, ad mare Caspium, situm erat. Hoc regnum destruxit circa A.C. 1400 Tamerlanes: ex cujus ruinis emerserunt regna Cafan, Astracan, &c, quod hodieque famosissimum est, Crimense sive Præcopense.
units.tr: The army of the Western Tartars under the leader Batu laid waste Russia, Hungary, Austria, Poland and Silesia, and in a very great battle defeated Duke Henry of Silesia. These Tartars founded a very vast kingdom, which was called Disthense, that is, Desert Tartary; all of Russia obeyed its kings. It was also called by another name, Zavothense, and lay across the Volga, toward the Caspian Sea. Around the year 1400 Tamerlane destroyed this kingdom. From its ruins arose the kingdoms of Kazan, Astrakhan, etc., and the kingdom of Crimea, or Perekop, which is still very famous today.

units.la: Secundum regnum Tartarorum fuit Schadajense, ad fluvium Oxum & Jaxarten supra Persiam, ita dictum à Schagadajo, tertio filio Schingyis Khan.
units.tr: The second Tartar kingdom was that of Chagatai, beside the rivers Oxus and Jaxartes beyond Persia. It was so named after Chagatai, the third son of Genghis Khan.

units.la: Tertium regnum fuit Persicum, quod constituit Ulakku-Khan, qui ultimum Califam seu Pontificem aracenorum Bagdadi captum fame inter medios thesauros necavit.
units.tr: The third kingdom was Persia, which was founded by Hulagu Khan, who starved to death the last caliph, or pontiff, of the Saracens, captured at Baghdad, shutting him up among his heaps of treasure.

units.la: Quartum regnum fuit Cathayæ, cujus Rex dicebatur Magnus Chan. Hujus Imperium cæteri omnes Tartarorum Reges agnoscebant.
units.tr: The fourth kingdom was that of Cathay, whose king was called the Great Khan. All the other Tartar kings acknowledged his empire.

units.la: Imperium Tartaricum instauravit Timurus sive Tamerlanes.
units.tr: Timurus, or Tamerlane, restored the Tartar empire.

units.la: Circa A. C. 1377, cum Tartarorum res mutuis dissidiis penitus collapsae essent, ... lapsæ fuissent, quidam Timurus latro, quod claudicaret dictus Lenck, i e, claudus, vulgò Tamerlanes, illud iterum ad summam potestatem & majestatem deduxit, universâ Asiâ debellatâ, solâ Sinâ exceptâ. Hic maximas res, atq; penè incredibiles, gessit: imprimis verò Bajazethem, Turcarum Imperatorem, maximô prælio victum ferreâ cavea inclusit, & ludibrio toti Asiæ circumduxit.
units.tr: Around the year 1377 AD, when the affairs of the Tartars had collapsed completely through mutual dissensions, a certain brigand named Timurus, called Lenck because he limped, that is, "the lame," commonly known as Tamerlane, brought it back to supreme power and majesty. He subdued all of Asia, except China alone. He achieved very great and almost incredible things. Above all, he defeated Bajazeth, Emperor of the Turks, in a great battle, shut him up in an iron cage, and led him around all Asia as an object of mockery.

units.la: Causa fuit mors Tamerlanis, quam secuta fuit defectio multarum nationum, & in primis Persarum & Turcarum.
units.tr: The cause was the death of Tamerlane, which was followed by the revolt of many nations, especially the Persians and the Turks.
The descendants of Tamerlane kept the kingdom of Chagatai and India.

units.la: Usq;ad A. C. 1500. Nam eò tempore regnum Schagadai occupatum fuit à qvodam Usbek, ita, ut hodie tota Schagadaja vocetur regnum Usbek.
units.tr: Until the year 1500 AD. For at that time the kingdom of Chagatai was seized by a certain Uzbek, so that today the whole of Chagatai is called the kingdom of the Uzbeks.

units.la: Posteri verò Tamerlanis fugerunt in Indiam, ibiqve A. C 1526 miris caedibus ingens illud imperium constituerunt, qvod hodieq; regnum Magni Majolis appellatur, cui potentia opibusq;, extra Sinam, in totâ Asiâ nemo par est.
units.tr: The descendants of Tamerlane, however, fled into India, and there, in the year 1526 AD, after great slaughter, established that vast empire, which today is called the kingdom of the Great Mogul, and outside China no one in all Asia is its equal in power and wealth.

units.la: Coepit bellum illud Tartaricum contra Sinenses A. C. 1616 Cau a fuit injuria Mercatoribus Tartaro-cum Orientalium à Sinensibus illata. Eam ulturi Tartari per murum in Si-nam penetrarunt, & maximum bel-lum moverunt, admirabili partium fortuna, donec A. C. 1644 regiam urbem Peking fraude expugnarent Tartari. Quod cum intellexisset Im-perator Sinensium Zungchinus [?], ar-repto gladio filiam nubilem obtrun-cavit, se ipsum vero de arbore pru-no fascia suspendit. Ita extincta fa-milia Imperatorum Sinensium Tar-tari tredecim provinciis potiti sunt, & eodem anno cunctas Tartarorum nationes ad expugnandas Sinensis Imperii reliquias evocarunt, inpri-mis vero remotissimas supralaponiā. Sic igitur innumerabilis Tartarorum multitudo universam Sinam inunda-vit, & ineffabilis maximarum ur-bium hominumque strages facta fuit. Nunc vero, ut novissimæ ex Sina literæ referunt, Tartari duas, quæ restabant, provincias quoq; expugnarunt, ut universum Sinense Imperium hodiè in Tartarorum po-testate sit, quorum Imperator, nomine Xunchi, novam regum familiam, Taicing dictam, condidit.
units.tr: That Tartar war against the Chinese began in A.D. 1616. Its cause was an injury done by the Chinese to Tartar and Eastern merchants. To avenge it, the Tartars broke through the wall into China and waged a great war with changing fortunes on both sides, until in A.D. 1644 the Tartars took the imperial city of Peking by treachery. When the Chinese emperor Zungchinus [?] learned of this, he seized a sword and cut down his marriageable daughter, and then hanged himself from a plum tree with a sash. So the imperial family of the Chinese was extinguished, and the Tartars took possession of thirteen provinces. In the same year they called all the Tartar nations together to conquer the remnants of the Chinese Empire, especially the most remote peoples beyond Lapland. Thus an countless multitude of Tartars flooded the whole of China, and an unspeakable slaughter of very great cities and peoples took place. Now, as the latest letters from China report, the Tartars have also conquered the two provinces that remained, so that the whole Chinese Empire is today in the power of the Tartars. Their emperor, named Xunchi, founded a new royal dynasty called Taicing.
The Slavonic is either Dalmatian or Sarmatian.

units.la: Inter amplissimas Orbis nationes Sclavi recensentur, quorum lingua hodieq; latissimè obtinet. Hæ Sclavorum gentes circa A. C. 584 se-dibus suis egressæ florentissima regna & Imperia condidere.
units.tr: Among the most extensive nations of the world the Slavs are counted, and their language still holds very wide sway today. These Slavic peoples, leaving their seats around A.D. 584, founded flourishing kingdoms and empires.

units.la: Regnum Dalmatiæ Croatiam, Serviam, Russiam, Bosniam & Bulgariam complectebatur. Ex-
units.tr: The kingdom of Dalmatia comprised Croatia, Serbia, Russia, Bosnia and Bulgaria. Ex-

units.la: A. C. 548 Ostrivog Rex Sclavo-rum cum sua gente occupavit Illyricum, cujus Nepos Seli, expugnata Scodra, Regem Dalmatiæ se appella-vit. Hujus regni tanta fuerunt in-crementa, ut tandem Stephanus circa A. C. 1340 Imperatorem Græciæ, Serviæ & Bulgariæ sese appellaverit. Sed paulo post circa A C. 1460 omnia hæc regna in potestatem Turcarum concesserunt.
units.tr: In A.D. 548 Ostrivog, king of the Slavs, with his people occupied Illyricum. His nephew Seli, after taking Scodra, called himself king of Dalmatia. The growth of this kingdom was so great that at last Stephen, around A.D. 1340, styled himself emperor of Greece, Serbia and Bulgaria. But shortly afterwards, around A.D. 1460, all these kingdoms passed into the power of the Turks.
The Sarmatian (scheme) is either Bohemian, or Polish, or Russian.

units.la: Salimin Dalmatiæ Rex tres fratres habuit: Czechium, Lechum, & Rusum, qui colonias Sclavorum & Illyricorum circa A. C. 1550 in Bohemiam, Moraviam, Poloniam & Rusiam duxerunt.
units.tr: Salimin, king of Dalmatia, had three brothers: Czechius, Lechus and Rusus, who led colonies of Slavs and Illyrians into Bohemia, Moravia, Poland and Russia around the year 1550 after Christ.

units.la: Bohemorum conditor fuit Czechins[?], à quo Bohemi suâ hodieque linguâ Czechi appellantur. Cumq; initio Duces suos habuissent, Henricus IV Imperator Uladislaum A.C. 1086 Regem Bohemorum creavit: quem titulum per 180 annos intermissum Uladislaus alius A.C. 1159 concedente Friderico Barbarossa, recepit, & ad posteros continuâ serie transmisit.
units.tr: The founder of the Bohemians was Czechins[?], from whom the Bohemians are still called Czechi in their own language. Although at first they had their own dukes, Henry IV the Emperor created Uladislaus king of the Bohemians in 1086; this title, lapsed for 180 years, was taken up again by another Uladislaus in 1159 with the consent of Frederick Barbarossa, and he handed it down to his descendants in an unbroken line.
The family of the Ottocars greatly distinguished Bohemia.

units.la: Premislaus, R ex Bohemiæ, qvod Imperatori Ottoni IV impensè fave-ret, dictus est Ottocarus, i e totus Ottonis; quem titulum posteri ipsius retinuerunt. Ex his Premislaus Ottocarus III Regnum Bohemiæ ad summam altitudinem perduxit, il-ludqve à mare Balthico usq; ad Adriaticum propagavit, occupatâ Austriâ, Carniolâ, Marchio Vinidorum, Slavoniâ, Stiriâ & Prussiâ. Superatis Tartaris urbem Königsbergam condidit. Sed omnes has provin-cias ipsi cum vitâ eripuit Imperator Rudolphus I Habsburgicus, condi-tor familiæ Austriacæ hodiernæ. Nihil igitur posteris Ottocari remansit, præter Bohemiam & Moraviam.
units.tr: Premislaus, king of Bohemia, because he strongly favoured the Emperor Otto IV, was called Ottocarus, that is, "wholly Otto's"; his descendants retained this title. Of these, Premislaus Ottocarus III brought the kingdom of Bohemia to its greatest height and extended it from the Baltic Sea to the Adriatic, having occupied Austria, Carniola, the Margraviate of the Windic Marches, Slavonia, Styria and Prussia. After defeating the Tartars he founded the city of Königsberg. But the Emperor Rudolf I of Habsburg, founder of the present Austrian house, snatched all these provinces from him along with his life. Nothing therefore remained to the descendants of Ottocar except Bohemia and Moravia.

units.la: Extinctâ Ottocarorum familiâ Regnum Bohemiæ ad exteros pervenit: primò quidem ad Iohannem Ducem Lutzenburgicum, cujus filius fuit Carolo IV Imperator, post quem Wenceslaus ignavus, & deinde Sigismundus regnaverunt. Ab his Bohemia ad domum Austriacam pervenit, quanquam interruptâ successione; quippe Ladislao posthumo repente extinctô Georgius Podjebra-tius, nobilis Bohemus, & deinde Ladislaus & Ludovicus ex Polonis regnarunt. Post has Bohemia denuò ad Austriacos rediit, & semel tantum uno anno ex Palatinis Fridericus regnavit. Quô mox debellatô Austriaci hactenus liberâ electione constituti Bohemiam hæreditarium regnum fecerunt.
units.tr: When the family of the Ottocars became extinct, the kingdom of Bohemia passed to foreigners: first indeed to John, Duke of Luxembourg, whose son was the Emperor Charles IV, after whom King Wenceslaus the Idle and then Sigismund reigned. From these the kingdom passed to the house of Austria, though the succession was interrupted; for when Ladislaus Posthumus suddenly died, George of Poděbrady, a Bohemian nobleman, and then Ladislaus and Louis, from the Poles, reigned. After these Bohemia returned again to the Austrians, and Frederick, from the Palatines, reigned for one year only. When he was soon defeated, the Austrians, who had hitherto been established by free election, made Bohemia a hereditary kingdom.

units.la: Polonorum gentem condidit Le-chus, frater Czechii & Rusi A.C.550 Hujus familiâ extinctâ successit A.C.700 Cracus, à quo Cracovia structa. Tertiam Principum familiam fundavit A.C.830 Rusticus quidam Piastus, qui diutissimè regnavit.
units.tr: Lechus, brother of Czechius and Rusus, founded the Polish nation, in about A.D. 550. After his family died out, Cracus succeeded in about A.D. 700, and Cracow was built by him. A rustic named Piastus founded a third ruling family in about A.D. 830, and it reigned for a very long time.

units.la: Poloniæ Primus Rex creatus fuit ab Ottone III Boleslaus Chobrius. Sed, cùm posteà Boleslaus Audax Sanctum Stanislaum Episcopum Cracovien-sem nefariè obtruncasset, Polonia per 115[?] annos titulo Regio abstinuit usq; ad A.C. 1295, quo Premislaus, post tàm diuturnum interregnum, Regium Diadema recepit, & ad posteros transmisit.
units.tr: Boleslaus Chobrius was created the first King of Poland by Otto III. But when Boleslaus the Bold had wickedly murdered Saint Stanislaus, bishop of Cracow, Poland abstained from the royal title for 115 [?] years, until A.D. 1295, when Premislaus, after so long an interregnum, received the royal diadem and handed it down to his descendants.
Silesia revolted from the King of Poland.

units.la: Autor defectionis fuit Henricus Dux Glogoviensis qui se, & omnes Silefiorum Ducatus, quorum 17, in clientelam Johannis Regis Bohemiæ, atq; ita imperio, tradidit: neq; ab eo tempore Poloni Silefiam recuperare potuerunt.
units.tr: The author of the revolt was Henry, Duke of Glogau, who surrendered himself and all the duchies of Silesia, of which there were 17, into the clientage of John, King of Bohemia, and so under the empire. From that time on, the Poles have been unable to recover Silesia.

units.la: A. C. 1368. Quippe, extincta familia Piasti Poloni, Jagellonem, Magnum Ducem Lithuaniæ, Regem suum crearunt, hac conditione, ut fidem Christianam amplecteretur, & Poloniæ Lithuaniam perpetuo jure conjungeret. Ita familia Jagellonidum, quæ in Poloni regnavit, extincta in Sigismundo Augusto A. C. 1570.
units.tr: In A.D. 1368. For when the family of the Polish Piasts died out, they made Jagiello, Grand Duke of Lithuania, their king, on the condition that he embrace the Christian faith and permanently join Lithuania to Poland. Thus the house of the Jagiellons, which reigned in Poland, died out with Sigismund Augustus in A.D. 1570.

units.la: A. C. 1466 Borussia in Casimiri Regis Poloniæ clientelam sese tradidit, & divisa fuit in Regium & Cruciferorum, quæ A. C. 1525. in Ducatum conversa, & Alberto Marchioni Brandeburgensi, ultimo Ordinis Teutonici Magistro, tradita fuit, à cujus posteritate hodieq; possidetur.
units.tr: In A.D. 1466 Prussia surrendered itself to the clientage of Casimir, King of Poland, and was divided into the Royal and the Cross-bearers parts. In A.D. 1525 it was turned into a duchy and handed over to Albert, Margrave of Brandenburg, the last Grand Master of the Teutonic Order; it is still possessed today by his descendants.

units.la: Sic quoq; Livonia A. C. 1561. ad Polonos concessit, ac abrogato Crucciferorum ordine Gothardus Ketlerus Dux Curlandiæ ac Semigalliæ creatus fuit. Reliquam Livoniam Polonis eripuerunt Sveci.
units.tr: Likewise, Livonia passed to the Poles in A.D. 1561, and with the Order of the Cross-bearers abolished, Gotthard Kettler was created Duke of Courland and Semigallia. The Swedes snatched the rest of Livonia from the Poles.

units.la: Extinctis Jagellonidis Polonia exteros Reges habere cœpit.
units.tr: After the Jagiellons died out, Poland began to have foreign kings.

units.la: A. C. 1573 Henricus Dux Andegavensis, Caroli IX Galliæ Regis frater, ter, à Polonis Rex creatus est, & in ejus locum, cùm fugâ se subduxis-set, surrogatus vit Stephanus Botho-reus, Transylvaniae Princeps. Eô fine prole mortuô Sigismundus, Johannis III Svevorum Regis filius, electus fuit, cujus posteritas usq; ad A. C. 1668 regnavit; qvô anno Johannes Casimirus Imperio se abdicavit, & ex prosapia Piastorum Michael Wiesnowvitz, post hujus verò obitum Johannes Sobieski A. C. 1674 Rex constitutus est.
units.tr: In A.D. 1573 Henry, Duke of Anjou, brother of Charles IX, King of France, was created king of the Poles three times; and when he had withdrawn by flight, Stephen Báthory, Prince of Transylvania, was put in his place. When he died without offspring, Sigismund, son of John III, King of the Swedes, was elected, and his line reigned until A.D. 1668. In that year John Casimir abdicated the throne, and Michael Wiśniowiecki of the Piast lineage was made king, and after his death John Sobieski was constituted king in A.D. 1674.

units.la: Polonia Sveciae conjuncta, & mox iterum ab ea divulsa fuit.
units.tr: Poland was united with Sweden, and soon after was again torn away from it.

units.la: Conjunctio Poloniae & Sveciae[?] facta fuit A. C. 1593, mortuo Johan-ne III Rege Svecorum. Huic filius Sigismundus Rex Poloniae suc-cessit: Sed cum is Jesuitas in Sveciam introduceret, & religionem turbaret, Sveci patruum ejus Carolum, Ducem Sudermanniæ, primo quidem gubernatorem, sed tandem A. C. 1607 Regem Sveciæ constituerunt, exclusâ penitus Sigismundi familiâ.
units.tr: The union of Poland and Sweden was made in A.D. 1593, on the death of John III, King of the Swedes. His son Sigismund, King of Poland, succeeded him. But since he introduced the Jesuits into Sweden and disturbed the religion, the Swedes made his uncle Charles, Duke of Södermanland, first governor, but finally, in A.D. 1607, King of Sweden, and Sigismund's family was completely excluded.
Poland was shaken by a huge upheaval.

units.la: A. C. 1647 Cosacci & Tartari Polonia & Lithuaniam horrendum in modum vastarunt, & deinceps Russis evocatis ipsorum imperio sese cum magna Ruffia Nigra & Ukrainæ parte submiserunt.
units.tr: In A.D. 1647 the Cossacks and Tartars devastated Poland and Lithuania in a horrible manner, and afterwards, having called in the Russians, they submitted themselves with a large part of Black Russia and Ukraine to their rule.
Russus, brother of Czech and Lech, founded the Russian people together with a part of the Slavs,

units.la: Sclavorum parte condiditRussorum gentem, sed ipsi Russi originem su-am deducunt à Waregis, per quos intelligunt qvicqvid nationum mari Balthico adjacet, nempe Finnos, Své-cos, Lives, Vandalos. Primus Rus-sorum Monarcha fuit Ruricus, circa A. C. 753. Ex ejus Successoribus fuit primus monarcha Svatoslaus si-ve Stoslaus, qvem Græci vocant Sphendostablum, qvi, domitâ Bulgariâ, Imperium Rufficum ad PontumEu-xinum & Traciam extendit. Post eum Russia in tres Ducatus diviſa, mox ad solum Vladimirum devenit, qvi, dućtâ Anii Basilii Imperatoris Constantinopolitani filiâ, religio-nem Christianam in Russiam intro-duxit A. C. 989. Cumq duodecim reliqvisset filios Russia in xii Ducatus divifla est, qvi varie inter se vel ite-rum conjuncti vel distracti sunt. Pręcipui autem Ducatus fuerunt Kiovia & Wolodimiria: qvorum illa Russia Ni-
units.tr: but the Russians themselves derive their origin from the Varegi, by whom they understand whatever nations border the Baltic Sea, namely the Finns, Swedes, Livonians and Vandals. The first monarch of the Russians was Ruricus, around A.D. 753. Among his successors the first monarch was Svatoslaus, or Stoslaus, whom the Greeks call Sphendostablus, who, after subduing Bulgaria, extended the Russian empire to the Black Sea and Thrace. After him Russia was divided into three duchies, but soon came under Vladimir alone, who, having married Anna, daughter of the Emperor Basil of Constantinople, introduced the Christian religion into Russia in A.D. 989. When he left twelve sons, Russia was divided into twelve duchies, which were variously joined together or separated again. The principal duchies were Kiev and Volodimir; of these, the former was regarded as the capital of Black Russia, the latter of White Russia.

units.la: 1. divisio. Nigræ, hæc Albæ caput habebatur.

A. C. 1224 Tartari Duce Bathi universam Russiam potestati suæ subjecerunt; quæ servitus usq; ad A. C. 1500 duravit. Tum tempo-ris enim Johannes Basilides primum Magnum Ducem omnium Rus-sorum appellavit, & Tartaros Ruf-fiâ expulit.
units.tr: In A.D. 1224 the Tartars, under their leader Bathi, subjected all of Russia to their power; this servitude lasted until A.D. 1500. At that time Johannes Basilides first called himself Grand Duke of all the Russians and drove the Tartars out of Russia.

units.la: Circa A. C. 1300 Poloni, captâ Kioviâ Russiam Nigram sibi subjecerunt, in quorum potestate mansit ad nostra usq; tempora, donec nuperrimè Luce Cossacorum Chmilenzki ad Moscovitas defecerunt.
units.tr: Around A.D. 1300 the Poles, having captured Kiev, subjected Black Russia to themselves. It remained under their power down to our own times, until most recently Luke Chmielnicki, leader of the Cossacks, went over to the Muscovites.

units.la: Ruffiæ Albæ caput Urbs Mo-scovia facta.
units.tr: The city of Moscow made the capital of White Russia.

units.la: Circa A. C. 1315 Daniel Dux Rufforum sedem Imperii ex urbe Wolodimiria Moscoviam transtu-lit; à quo tempore & Ruffia Mosco-via, & Ruffæ Moscovita appellan-tur.
units.tr: Around A.D. 1315 Daniel, Duke of the Russians, moved the seat of empire from the city of Volodimir to Moscow; from this time Russia is called Muscovia, and the Russians Muscovites.
The Russian empire is extended most widely.

units.la: Qvippe Johannes Basilides Magnam Novogardiam A. C. 1477 occupavit, ejusq; Successor Basilius A. C. 1518 provincias Glaciali Oceano vicinas usq; ad fluvium Obij & Novam Cemblam occupavit. Ducatus quoq; Smolensco & Plescoviæ expugnavit, unde Tzar, i e. Imperator dictus fuit. Sub Johanne Basilide II duo Regna Tartarica Cafan & Astra-can accesserc. Ita imperium Mo-scoviticum usq; ad mare Caspium & Persiæ fines prolatum fuit.
units.tr: Indeed, Johannes Basilides occupied Great Novgorod in A.D. 1477, and his successor Basilius in A.D. 1518 occupied the provinces bordering the Glacial Ocean as far as the river Ob and Nova Zembla. He also conquered Smolensk and Pskov, whence he was called Tzar, that is, Emperor. Under Johannes Basilides II the two Tartar kingdoms of Kazan and Astrakhan were added. Thus the Muscovite empire was extended as far as the Caspian Sea and the borders of Persia.
Michael Fedrowvitz founded the new dynasty of the Russian emperors.

units.la: A. C. 1612, post horrendas illas in Russia confusiones, qvas nebulo qvidam Gregorius Strepium, gerens se pro Demetrio Johannis Basilidis filio, excitaverat, Russi tandem Magnum Ducem crearunt Michaelem Fedrowvitz, qvi Russiæ imperium miserrimè afflictum prudentia, moderatione, ac perpetuâ cum vicinis pace, recreavit, & unam tantum eamq; atrocem cladem à Polonis A. C. 1634 in obsidione urbis Smolenfco accepit. Ei A. C. successit filius Alexium Michaelovvitz, qvém A.C. 1675 Fœdor Alexovvitz, sedecim annorum filius, secutus est.
units.tr: In the year of our Lord 1612, after those dreadful disorders in Russia, which a certain scoundrel named Gregory Strepius had stirred up by passing himself off as Demetrius, son of John Basilides, the Russians at last made Michael Fedrowvitz grand duke. He restored the Russian empire, which had been most wretchedly afflicted, by his prudence, moderation and constant peace with his neighbours; and he suffered only one cruel defeat, at the hands of the Poles during the siege of the city of Smolensk in the year of our Lord 1634. He was succeeded in the year of our Lord by his son Alexius Michaelovitz, whom in 1675 Feodor Alexovitz, a sixteen-year-old son, followed.

units.la: [?]Æthiopica est vel Arabica, vel Africana, vel Indica.
units.tr: The Ethiopian [history] is either Arabian, or African, or Indian.

units.la: Per Æthiopes intelligimus omnes illas nationes, qvæ sub Zona torrida habitant, & colore fusco vel nigro sunt tincti.
units.tr: By Ethiopians we understand all those nations which live under the torrid zone and are tinged with a dark or black colour.
The Arabs founded a very extensive empire.

units.la: A.C. 622 Arabes sive Saraceni, Duce Mahumede, qui se Prophetam jactabat, eruptione facta amplissimi Imperii fundamenta jecerunt. Ejus fucsuccessores dicti sunt Chalifæ, i.e. Vicarii vel summi Pontifices; & E-miri[?] erant Præfecti Imperii. Africâ, Cypro, Rhodo cum Galliæ parte potiti à Sina usq; ad Herculis Columnas cuncta terrarum nationumq; in mores, lingvam, religionemque suam corruperunt.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 622 the Arabs, or Saracens, under their leader Mahomet, who boasted that he was a prophet, broke out and laid the foundations of a very extensive empire. His successors were called Caliphs, that is, vicars or supreme pontiffs; and the Emirs were the prefects of the empire. They seized Africa, Cyprus, Rhodes and part of Gaul, and from the Sina to the Pillars of Hercules they corrupted all the lands and nations in their manners, language and religion.

units.la: Divisum fuit in V Chalifa-tus: Andalusiæ, Fessæ, Kairoüanni, Ægypti & Bagdadi.
units.tr: It was divided into five caliphates: Andalusia, Fez, Kairouan, Egypt and Baghdad.

units.la: Hæc divisio cœpit A.C. 756. Et hac ratione inexpugnabilis illa imperii Saracenici moles dissipata inu-tilibus bellis debilitata fuit.
units.tr: This division began in the year of Christ 756. By this means that unconquerable mass of the Saracen empire was broken up and weakened by useless wars.
The Ommiads founded the caliphate of Andalusia.

units.la: Per Andalufiam Arabes intelligunt Hispaniam, Ommiadæ fuerunt posteri Ommiæ, quæ erat factio religiosa & politica inter Arabes. Se-deshujus Chalifatus fuit Corduba.
units.tr: By Andalusia the Arabs mean Spain. The Ommiads were descendants of Ommia, a religious and political faction among the Arabs. The seat of this caliphate was Cordova.
It was divided into very many kingdoms.

units.la: Circa A.C. 1030, extincta penitus familia Ommiadum singularum urbium Præfecti per Hispaniam se Reges constituerunt, ita, ut XIX regna Saracenica in Hispania numerarentur, quorum hæc sunt nomina: Saragossa, Balaqueris, Montionis, Barbastri, Fraga, Albarracini, Dia-nii, Tudela, Majorica, Osca, Toleti, Murcia, Almeria, Pacis Augustæ, Portugallia, Sevilia, Corduba, Granada & Ilenda. Ex his solum Granadæ regnum Mauris remansit; quod demum A. C. 1492, captâ Gra-nadâ, à Ferdinando, Rege Hispaniæ, excisum fuit. Ita Saracenorum jugo, cùm per annos 700 eam infcedissent, liberata tandē fuit Hispania.
units.tr: Around the year of Christ 1030, when the family of the Ommiads had completely died out, the prefects of the individual cities throughout Spain made themselves kings, so that nineteen Saracen kingdoms were counted in Spain, whose names are these: Saragossa, Balaguer, Monzón, Barbastro, Fraga, Albarracín, Denia, Tudela, Majorca, Huesca, Toledo, Murcia, Almería, Badajoz, Portugal, Seville, Cordova, Granada and Elvira. Of these, only the kingdom of Granada remained to the Moors; this was finally cut down in the year of Christ 1492, when Granada was taken by Ferdinand, King of Spain. Thus Spain was at last freed from the yoke of the Saracens, under whose subjection it had languished for 700 years.
Idris founded the Caliphate of Fez.

units.la: A. C. 788. Hic Jdris ex familiâ Omniadum fuit, & Mauritaniam cum suâ Secta occupavit, conditâ urbe Fesur.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 788. This Idris was of the family of the Omniads, and occupied Mauritania with his sect, having founded the city of Fez.

units.la: Hi Saraceni occuparunt Cretam, Siciliam, Sardiniam, Corsicam, Maltam & Italiæ partem.
units.tr: These Saracens occupied Crete, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, Malta and part of Italy.

units.la: Ita, ut omnes penè Maris Mediterranei Insulæ in potestatem illo-
units.tr: So that almost all the islands of the Mediterranean Sea came under their power.

units.la: Erum concederent. In Creta condiderunt urbem Candiam, à qva tota Insula hodie Candia appellatur.
units.tr: In Crete they founded the city of Candia, from which the whole island is today called Candia.
Canon I. The Zenatae gain the caliphate.

units.la: A. C. 975 Zeira, filius Athiæ Zenatæus, deletâ familiâ Idris Chalifatum Mauritaniæ obtinuit. Hi Zenatæi divisi fuerant in duas stirpes, Mecnasam & Magraoam, quæ ordine imperarunt.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 975, Zeira, son of Athia the Zenatan, having destroyed the family of Idris, obtained the caliphate of Mauritania. These Zenatae were divided into two branches, the Mecnasa and the Magraoa, which held power in turn.
The Lontunii Almoravids drove out the Zenatae.

units.la: A. C. 1052 Lontunii Africæ populus Zenatos Mauritaniæ imperio pepulerunt. Primus Lontuniorum Chalifa fuit Abul Tesfevin. Ei successit Joseph, qui universam Africam cam[?] usq; adÆgyptum & Nigritarum regionem, cum universi Hispanis, domuit & Monarcha transmarinus & cismarinus factus est. Hic con-didit urbem Marucco, quæ in poste-rum[?] imperii sedes fuit.
units.tr: In the year 1052 AD the people of the Lontunii in Africa drove the Zenatae from power over Mauritania. The first caliph of the Lontunii was Abul Tesfevin. He was succeeded by Joseph, who subdued all of Africa as far as Egypt and the region of the Nigritae, together with all of Spain, and became a monarch on both sides of the sea. He founded the city Marucco, which afterwards became the seat of the empire.

units.la: A. C. 1139 quidam Ludimagi-ster, cui nomen Elmahadi, spe reli-gionis reformandæ Africæ & Hispa-niæ, Pontificatu potitus est. Cujus Successores, inprimis Jacob Alman-sor, omnium latissimè imperarunt.
units.tr: In the year 1139 AD a certain schoolmaster, named Elmahadi, gained the leadership in the hope of reforming religion in Africa and Spain. His successors, above all Jacob Almansor, ruled over the widest territories of all.

units.la: Circa A. C. 1210. Causa hujus mumutationis fuit ingens illa clades, qvam Mahumed Ennasir in Hispania ad Navas Tolofanas accepit, amissis suorum 20000. Sic amissa Hispani profugus in Africam, ibi paulò post mœrore animi extinctus, filios inter se pro imperio discordes reliquit. Ita imperium Almohadā-rum[?] in varia regna minora dissipa-tum dilaceratumque fuit, ex quibus præcipua erant: Granadense in Hispania, Tunetanum & Tremesenum in Africa.
units.tr: Around the year 1210 AD. The cause of this change was that great defeat which Mahumed Ennasir suffered in Spain at Navas Tolofanas, with the loss of 20,000 of his men. Having lost them, the Spaniard fled into Africa, where, soon afterwards, he died of grief, leaving his sons at odds with one another over the empire. Thus the empire of the Almohads was broken up and torn apart into various smaller kingdoms, of which the chief were: the Granadense in Spain, and the Tunetanum and Tremesenum in Africa.

units.la: Ipsam vero Mauritaniam sive regnum Fessæ & Marucco obtinuit qvi-dam Buccar Marinus, cujus succes-sores dicti Marinei.
units.tr: Mauritania itself, that is the kingdom of Fez and Marucco, was taken by a certain Buccar Marinus, and his successors were called the Marinei.
The Merinids were succeeded by the Oat-

units.la: A. C. 1480 familia Qvattas sive Oattas Mauritaniam occupavit, & in eâ variâ fortunâ usque ad A. C. 1548 regnavit.
units.tr: In A.D. 1480 the family of the Quattas, or Oattas, occupied Mauritania and ruled in it, with varying fortune, until A.D. 1548.

units.la: A.C. 1500 quidam Hamed Scheriphius, prætextu religionis, regnum Maroccanum occupavit. Cui successit frater Mahumed, qui, extincto Hamede, ultimo ex familia Oattas, totius Mauritaniæ Imperium solus obtinuit A.C. 1548.
units.tr: In A.D. 1500 a certain Hamed Scherif, under the pretext of religion, seized the kingdom of Morocco. He was succeeded by his brother Mahumed, who, after Hamed, the last of the family of the Oattas, was killed, obtained sole control of the whole empire of Mauritania in A.D. 1548.

units.la: Dissidium inter Scheriphios regnum Portugalliæ gravissimè afflixit.
units.tr: The dissension among the Scherifs grievously afflicted the kingdom of Portugal.

units.la: Nam cum Sebastianus, Portugal-liæ Rex, sese dissidentibus Scheriphiis immisceret, A. C.1578 cum totâ exercitu periit, & florentissimum Portugalliæ regnum ita debilitavit, ut id Philippus II, Rex Hispaniæ, non magno negotio occuparet.
units.tr: For when Sebastian, King of Portugal, interfered in the quarrel between the Scherifs, he perished with his whole army in A.D. 1578. He so weakened the flourishing kingdom of Portugal that Philip II, King of Spain, occupied it without much difficulty.

units.la: Scheriphii perpetuo inter se discordes sunt.
units.tr: The Scherifs are always at odds with one another.

units.la: Causa est controversia inter patruos & nepotes de successione.
units.tr: The cause is a dispute between uncles and nephews over the succession.
Hamed Beridalla did indeed rebel against them.

units.la: A.C.1612 quidam impostor artibus magicis Scheriphios Mauritaniâ pepulit, sed paulo post superatus periit. Hodie imperium Mauritaniæ tenet Mahumed Turcarum Imperator.
units.tr: In A.D. 1612 a certain impostor, by magic arts, drove the Scherifs out of Mauritania, but was soon defeated and died. Today the empire of Mauritania is held by Mahumed, Emperor of the Turks.
The Caliphate of Kairovvan was held by the sons of Aglab.

units.la: Hic Chalifatus complectebatur interiorem Africam. Hujus familiæ Aglab res admodum in Historiis obscuræ sunt, nisi quæ feruntur crebram in Siciliam & vicinas Insulas pi-raticam exercuisse.
units.tr: This Caliphate embraced inland Africa. The affairs of this family of Aglab are very obscure in the histories, except that they are reported to have frequently carried on piracy against Sicily and the neighbouring islands.
The Caliphs of Kairovvan gained possession of Egypt and Syria.

units.la: Post familiam Aglab quidam Ab-dalla cognomento Mahdi i.e. com-planator, originem suam à Fatima, filia Mahumedis, ducens Chalifatum KairoKairovvanæ occupavit. Cujus successores Ægypto expugnatâ condide-runt urbem Alcahiram, quæ inposterum sedes Imperii & Chalifatus fuit.
units.tr: After the family of Aglab, a certain Abdalla, surnamed Mahdi, that is, the guide, tracing his origin to Fatima, the daughter of Mahomet, seized the Caliphate of Kairovvan. His successors, after conquering Egypt, founded the city of Cairo, which afterwards became the seat of the Empire and of the Caliphate.

units.la: Canon. Chalifatus Ægypti pervenit ad Sultanos. Explicatio 1.
units.tr: Canon. The Caliphate of Egypt passed to the Sultans. Explanation 1.

units.la: Extinctâ Fatimidarum familiâ in Ægypto, loco Chalifarum, Sultani sive Imperatores regnarunt: primò quidem Mahmudus, cognomento Nu-radin; ei successit Sahladinus, conditor familiæ Ajobidarum i. e. ex posteritate Jobi. Nam Sahladinus originem suam referebat ad Jobum illum patientem,
units.tr: With the family of the Fatimids extinct in Egypt, Sultans, or emperors, reigned in place of the Caliphs: first Mahmud, surnamed Nuradin; he was succeeded by Saladin, founder of the family of the Ayyubids, that is, of the posterity of Job. For Saladin traced his origin back to that Job, the patient one,

units.la: Extinctâ Ajobitarum familiâ successerunt Turcomanni A. C 1250[?] longâ serie.
units.tr: With the Ayyubid family extinct, the Turkomans succeeded, through a long series [of rulers], in about 1250[?] A.D.

units.la: Hi imperio exuti fuerunt à mancipiis suis Mamaluccis seu Circassis A. C. 1381[?]. Inter hos Mamaluccos ultimus fuit Tomumbejus[?], occisus à Turcis, ut suprà dictum.
units.tr: These were stripped of power by their slaves, the Mamelukes or Circassians, in about 1381[?] A.D. Among these Mamelukes the last was Tomumbey[?], killed by the Turks, as mentioned above.
The Caliphate of Bagdad was retained by the Abbasids.

units.la: Cum ita defecissent Africani & Hispani à familia Abbasidarum, ea Chalifatum Bagdadensem, i.e. Persiam, & Orientem, retinuit varia fortunâ. Cumq; Præfecti provinciarum passim rebellarent, magis magisq;, potentia & autoritas Chalifarum Bagdadensium debilitata fuit; ita, ut tandem, amissâ omni regiâ & politicâ potestate, solam rerum Ecclesiasticarum curam retinuerint. Penitus autem deleti fuére Chalifæ Bagdaden-ses a Tartaris A. C. 1260, ut supra sub Tit. Imperii Tartarici, in fine Periodi 1. dictum.
units.tr: When the Africans and Spaniards had thus broken away from the family of the Abbasids, that family retained the Caliphate of Bagdad, that is, Persia and the East, with varying fortune. As the governors of the provinces rebelled here and there, the power and authority of the Caliphs of Bagdad were more and more weakened, until at last, having lost all royal and political power, they kept only the care of ecclesiastical affairs. The Caliphs of Bagdad were utterly destroyed by the Tartars in A.D. 1260, as said above under the title Tartar Empire, at the end of Period 1.

units.la: A. C. 932 Filiæ Boya, qvi genus ducebant ex prisci Persarum regibus, adeoq; ab ipso Dario Hystaspis filio, imperium Persiæ occupaverunt, & Chalifatum omni potestate politica spoliarunt. His Boytis in imperio successerunt Turcæ, ut supra dictum in Period. 1. Impor. Turcici.
units.tr: In A.D. 932 the sons of Boya, who traced their descent from the ancient kings of the Persians, and so from Darius son of Hystaspes himself, seized the empire of Persia and stripped the Caliphate of all political power. The Boyids were succeeded in the empire by the Turks, as said above in Period 1 of the Turkish Empire.

units.la: Africana est vel Abyssina, vel Nigritica, vel Congensis, vel Monomotapana.
units.tr: The African realm is either Abyssinian, or Nigritic, or Congolese, or Monomotapan.

units.la: Imperium Abyssinum an-te aliquot secula potentissimū fuit.
units.tr: The Abyssinian empire was very powerful some centuries ago.

units.la: De Origine Abyssynorum certi ni-hil constat: sunt enim in Arabia Fe-lici ejusdem nominis gentes, ut in-certum sit ex Æthiopia in Arabiam, an ex Arabia in Æthiopiam migra-rint.
units.tr: Nothing certain is known about the origin of the Abyssinians. There are peoples of the same name in Arabia Felix, so it is uncertain whether they migrated from Ethiopia into Arabia or from Arabia into Ethiopia.

units.la: Ipsi Abyssini sese origine Chal-dæos profitentur, quod vero non ab-similē est; quandoquidem ex Assy-ria in Æthiopiam coloniam dedu-ctam testatur Nicephorus l. 9. c. 18. & Scaliger de Emend. temp. l. 6. c. 3. Antiquissimæ ipsorum & res & reges ignorantur. Extat quidem Catalogus regum Abyssinorum à Christo Noachi filio deductus, sed suspectæ fidei. Sub Justiniano I. Imperatore Rex Æthiopum Axumitatum[?] Adad sive David commemoratus, quod fidem Christianam recepit. Post ipsum incognita & inaccessa nobis mane-bat Abyssinia, & non nisi fabulis pe-regrinantium jactabatur. Circa A.{a} C. 1200 quidam Æthiopum Christianorum potentissimus Imperator, Papa vel Presbyter Johannes, (ex Persica voce Prester Chan i. e. Rex mancipiorum: nam mancipia Abyssena[?] toto Oriente frequentissima sunt) memorabatur, cujus regno incomparabilem felicitatem, qualem Poëtæ hortis Hesperidum, adscribebant.
units.tr: The Abyssinians themselves profess a Chaldean origin, and this is not an unlikely claim, since Nicephorus (l. 9. c. 18.) and Scaliger (de Emend. temp. l. 6. c. 3.) testify that a colony was led from Assyria into Ethiopia. Their most ancient affairs and kings are unknown. There is indeed a catalogue of Abyssinian kings traced back to Cham, son of Noah, but its reliability is doubtful. Under the Emperor Justinian I, a king of the Ethiopians, Axumitarum[?] Adad, or David, is mentioned, who received the Christian faith. After him Abyssinia remained unknown and inaccessible to us, and was talked about only in the tales of travellers. Around the year 1200 a certain most powerful Christian emperor of the Ethiopians, called Papa or Presbyter John (from the Persian word Prester Chan, that is, king of slaves, for slaves from Abyssinia are very common throughout the East), was reported, and to his kingdom people ascribed an incomparable happiness, such as the poets ascribed to the gardens of the Hesperides.

units.la: Circa A. C. 1500 Lusitani ex In-dia diaOrientali Abysiniam detexerunt: & quanquam jam A.C. 1400 Zarah Jacob, Rex Abysinorum, Legatos suos Romam ad Papam Eugenium IV misisset, tum tamen nihil adhuc certi de rebus Imperii innotuit, & Europæis usq; ad Lusitanorum ad-ventum inaccessa mansit. Abeo tem-pore, quò Lusitani Indiam Orientalem frequentarunt exactius omnia explorata; sed initia multis figmentis contaminata sunt; cum ipsi Aby-sini felicitatem & potentiam suam immane quantum extollerent men-daciter, ut innumera mendacia de A-bysinorum rebus vulgò spargeren-tur.
units.tr: Around 1500 the Portuguese, coming from India by way of the East, discovered Abyssinia. And although as early as 1400 Zara Jacob, king of the Abyssinians, had sent his envoys to Rome to Pope Eugenius IV, still nothing certain about the affairs of the empire was known at that time, and it remained inaccessible to Europeans until the arrival of the Portuguese. From that time, when the Portuguese frequented the East Indies, everything was explored more accurately; but the beginnings were contaminated by many fictions, since the Abyssinians themselves, lying, extolled their happiness and power to an immense degree, so that countless lies about Abyssinian affairs were spread abroad.

units.la: Quæ autem certò cognita sunt ab A.C. 1560 ita se habent: Abysi-nium Imperium olim 16 Regna, in 14 distributa Regiones, complectebatur: sed ita decrevit antiqua illa po-tentia & majestas, ut hodie non nisi 4. nimirum Tigris, Abagamediri, Dambea & Goroma ipsis parcant; reliqua omnia vel à Turcis, vel ab Afris, occupata sunt. Et indies magis magisq; decrescit Abysfinorum potentia, ut hodie vix ulla ipsorum ratio habeatur.
units.tr: What has been known for certain since 1560 is as follows. The Abyssinian empire once embraced sixteen kingdoms, divided into fourteen provinces; but that ancient power and majesty has declined so far that today only four, namely Tigre, Abagamedri, Dambea and Goroma, are left to them; all the rest have been occupied either by the Turks or by the Africans. And the power of the Abyssinians declines more and more every day, so that today hardly any account is taken of them.

units.la: Nigritæ in X V regna divi-si fuerunt.
units.tr: The Nigritae were divided into fifteen kingdoms.

units.la: Nigritæ sunt illi Æthiopes, qui in Lybia interiore fluvia Gir sive Nigir & Senegam accolunt. Hi cum olim subessent imperio Regum Mauritaniæ ex familia Lontuniorum Almoravidarum, postea ab illis deficientes in X V regna divisi fuere, quorum nomina hæc sunt: Gvalata, Ginea, Melli; Tombuto, Gago, Guber, Agades, Cano, Casenas, Zegzeg, Zanfara, Gvangara, Borni, Gaogo, Nubia. Ex his præcipuæ Nubia & Ginea; nihil autem vel admodum parum de ipsorum rebus constat.
units.tr: The Nigritae are those Ethiopians who dwell in interior Libya along the rivers Gir or Nigir and Senegal. Although they were once subject to the rule of the kings of Mauritania, of the family of the Lontunian Almoravids, they later revolted from them and were divided into fifteen kingdoms, whose names are these: Gvalata, Ginea, Melli; Tombuto, Gago, Guber, Agades, Cano, Casenas, Zegzeg, Zanfara, Gvangara, Borni, Gaogo, Nubia. Of these the chief are Nubia and Ginea; but little or nothing is known of their affairs.

units.la: Insularum Fortunatarum singulæ suos Reges vel Duces habuêre.
units.tr: Each of the Fortunate Islands had its own kings or leaders.

units.la: Insulæ Fortunatæ, collapso Imperio Romano, inaccessæ & incognitæ manserunt usq; ad A.C. 1370, quo Hispani eas iterum aperuerunt. Tunc temporis ea incolarum simplicitas fuit, ut igne & ferro, duabus ad vitam humanam maximè necessariis rebus, carerent. Quælibet Insula peculiarem linguam ac regimen habebat. Præcipua earum fuit Magna Canaria, divisa in duo regna, Theldæ & Gal-ria, & Galderæ. In illa A.C. 1430 quidam nomine Doramas, in hac Guauarta-ma regnabat. Insula Teneriffa Du-ces habuit novem liberâ electione succedentes.
units.tr: The Fortunate Islands, after the collapse of the Roman Empire, remained inaccessible and unknown until around A.D. 1370, when the Spaniards opened them up again. At that time the inhabitants were so simple that they lacked fire and iron, the two things most necessary for human life. Each island had its own language and government. The chief of them was Magna Canaria, divided into the two kingdoms of Theldae and Gal-ria, and Galderae. In the former, a certain man named Doramas was reigning in A.D. 1430, and in the latter Guauarta-ma. The island of Teneriffa had dukes who succeeded one another by free election, nine in number.

units.la: Regnum Insularum Fortunatarum à Francis occupatum fuit.
units.tr: The kingdom of the Fortunate Islands was occupied by the French.

units.la: Circa A.C. 1370 Robinus de Bracamonte, Franciæ Architalassus, has insulas pro filio suo Johanne de Betancourt regio titulo impetravit: qui, debellatis Barbaris, regem Canariæ, Lanzarotta, Fortaventuræ, Gomeræ, & Ferro se appellavit. Cui ordine succedêre Menardus, Petrus Barbæ, Ferdinandus Beraza & Didacus de Herrera, qui omne jus suum transtulit ad Ferdinandum Regem Hispaniæ; niæ; à quo tempore Insulæ Canariæ imperii Hispanici pars fuerunt.
units.tr: Around A.D. 1370, Robin de Bracamonte, Architalassus of France, obtained these islands with a royal title for his son John de Betancourt, who, having subdued the Barbarians, called himself king of the Canaries, Lanzarotta, Fortaventura, Gomera and Ferro. In order of succession he was followed by Menardus, Peter Barbae, Ferdinand Beraza and Didacus de Herrera, who transferred all his right to Ferdinand, King of Spain; from which time the Canary Islands have been part of the Spanish empire.
The kingdoms of Congo were united.

units.la: Cùm singulæ provinciæ singulos haberent Reges, tandem universæ in unius regis Bembæ[?] potestatem concesserunt: quod diu ante A. C. 1400 factum fuisse constat.
units.tr: Although the individual provinces each had their own kings, at last they all conceded power to one king of Bemba[?]; this is known to have happened long before A.D. 1400.

units.la: Hoc regnum antiqvo & vero nomine appellatur Ambonda. Circa A. C. 1500 qvidam Æthiops nomine Angola, auxilio Lusitanorum, cæteros Regulos debellavit, & sese Monarcham constituit: a cujus nomine regio est Angola dicta. Huic ob rerum gestarum magnitudinem cognomen Ngenc[?], i e. Magnus, datum. Tanta hujus potentia fuit, ut 1000000. hominum in aciem perducere potuerit.
units.tr: This kingdom is called by its ancient and true name Ambonda. Around A.D. 1500 a certain Ethiopian named Angola, with the help of the Portuguese, defeated the other petty kings and made himself monarch; the kingdom of Angola is named after him. He was given the surname Ngenc[?], that is, Great, on account of the greatness of his deeds. So great was his power that he was able to bring 1,000,000 men into the field.
The Agages or Jacchas destroyed the kingdom of Congo.

units.la: Occasio hujus calamitatis fuit fides Christiana, qvàm Reges Congo, svasu Lusitanorum, suscèperunt; & abalienatio Subditorum, & defectio provinciarum, secuta fuit. Tandem Agages sive Jacchas[?], populus interioris Africæ ferocissimus, A.C. 1560 in regnum Congo irruperunt, illudque ingenti cæde exhaustum penitus destruxerunt. Ab eo tempore Congenses se nunquam recolligere potuere.
units.tr: The occasion of this calamity was the Christian faith, which the kings of Congo received at the urging of the Portuguese; there followed the alienation of the subjects and the defection of the provinces. At last the Agages or Jacchas[?], the most savage people of the interior of Africa, invaded the kingdom of Congo in A.D. 1560 and, having drained it by great slaughter, utterly destroyed it. From that time the Congolese were never able to recover themselves.
Monomotapa is divided into four kingdoms.

units.la: Verum Monomotapæ nomen est Mocaranga, quæ olim uni Monarchæ suberat; sed superiori seculo imperator, cum se tot regnis gubernandis imparem videret, inter quatuor filios eadem distribuit, & majori natu dedit regnum Monomotapa, secundo regnum Quideva, tertio Sedanda, & quarto Chicanga.
units.tr: The true name of Monomotapa is Mocaranga, which was formerly subject to a single monarch. But in the last century the emperor, seeing that he was unequal to governing so many kingdoms, divided them among his four sons. He gave the eldest the kingdom of Monomotapa, the second the kingdom of Quideva, the third Sedanda, and the fourth Chicanga.

units.la: Præter hæc majora regna Æthiopum Africanorum regna innumera minora alia sunt, cum singulæ ferè urbes, imò pagi, singulos reges habeant, ex quibus celebriora sunt: Buttua, Sophala, Qviola, Batra, Prava, Magadoxo, Angoscia, Moxemuga, Mombaza, Melinda, Monsia, Zan-zibar, Madagascar, & plurima alia, quæ communi nomine vocantur re-gna Cassarum, i. e. infidelium, quod illorum incolæ sint adhuc Idololatræ & Pagani.
units.tr: Besides these larger kingdoms of the Ethiopians of Africa, there are countless smaller ones, since nearly every town, indeed every village, has its own king. The more famous of these are Buttua, Sophala, Quiola, Batra, Prava, Magadoxo, Angoscia, Moxemuga, Mombaza, Melinda, Monsia, Zanzibar, Madagascar, and very many others. Together they are called by the common name of the kingdoms of the Cassares, that is, of the unbelievers, because their inhabitants are still idolaters and heathens.
India is subject to countless kings.

units.la: India, præter continentem, innu-meras alias complectitur insulas, im-perio regibusque divisas, ut eorum numerus vel ratio nequeat iniri.
units.tr: India, besides the mainland, embraces countless other islands, divided by empire and kings, so that their number or reckoning cannot be ascertained.

units.la: Schabek imperium Kunkam in VI. regna divisit.
units.tr: Schabek divided the empire of Kunkam into six kingdoms.

units.la: Hic Schabek circa A. C. 1500 potentissimum Imperium in India condidit, ejusque majorem partem ditione complexus fuit, dictus alio nomine S. ha-Holam, i. e. Rex Mundi. Hujus Imperium in VI. regna divisum fuit, quorum
units.tr: This Schabek, about the year 1500 after Christ, founded a very powerful empire in India and brought under his rule most of it. He was also called by another name, S. ha-Holam, that is, King of the World. His empire was divided into six kingdoms, of which:

units.la: 1. Decan, cujus reges communiter appellantur Imad-Maluco, i. e. columna regni; pro quo Lusitani vitiosè pronunciant Madre-Maluco.
units.tr: 1. Decan, whose kings are commonly called Imad-Maluco, that is, pillar of the kingdom. The Portuguese wrongly pronounce this as Madre-Maluco.

units.la: 2. Amdenager, cujus reges vocantur Nisa-Maluco, i. e. regni hasta.
units.tr: 2. Amdenager, whose kings are called Nisa-Maluco, that is, the spear of the kingdom.

units.la: 3. Braganadar. Cujus reges vocantur Cotteb Maluco, i. e. vertex regni.
units.tr: 3. Braganadar, whose kings are called Cotteb Maluco, that is, the summit of the kingdom.

units.la: 4. Proprio caret nomine, cujus primus rex nomine Verido, natione Hungarus, A. C. 1510. obiit.
units.tr: 4. Has no name of its own. Its first king, named Verido, a Hungarian by birth, died in the year 1510 after Christ.
5. Vizapor, whose king was called Mu-hadum Koja.

units.la: 6. Goa[?], cujus primus Rex appel-latus fuit Sabeb Adelkan, i.e. Domi-nus, Rex justitiæ, ex quo Portugalli fecerunt Sabajo & Hidalkan.
units.tr: 6. Goa[?], whose first king was called Sabeb Adelkan, that is, Lord, King of Justice. From this the Portuguese made Sabajo and Hidalkan.

units.la: Canon. Regnum Malabar divisum in varia Regna. Explicatio:
units.tr: Canon. The kingdom of Malabar divided into various kingdoms. Explanation:

units.la: Regnum Malabar ante multa se-cula uni Monarchæ subjectum fuit, quorum ultimus Sarama Perymal circa A. C. 900, cùm liberis careret, regnum suum inter fidelissimos Ministrorum distribuit. vid. Scalig. de Emendat. temp. lib. 7. Ex his impe-rium rium in cæteros obtinuit Rex Calecuti, dictus Zamorus i.e Imperator: cui subjecta erant minora regna Cochin, Canonor, Baticola, Chala, Onor & Culon, cum aliis minoribus quibusdam.
units.tr: The kingdom of Malabar was subject to one monarch for many centuries. The last of them, Sarama Perymal, about the year 900 after Christ, having no children, distributed his kingdom among his most faithful ministers. See Scaliger, De emendatione temporum, book 7. From these, the king of Calecuti, called Zamorus, that is, Emperor, gained rule over the rest. Under him were the lesser kingdoms of Cochin, Canonor, Baticola, Chala, Onor and Culon, together with certain other smaller ones.
The principal kingdoms of Narsinga are: Negapatan, Maliapur, Bisnagar, Orixa.

units.la: Quem tractum Nautæ vulgò vo-cant Choromandel, & is complectitur regna Narsinga, quæ etiam Bisnagar appellantur. Regis Narsingæ tanta perhibetur esse potentia, ut regnum ejus vix intra sex menses circumiri possit.
units.tr: Sailors commonly call this region Choromandel, and it includes the kingdoms of Narsinga, which are also called Bisnagar. The power of the king of Narsinga is said to be so great that his kingdom can scarcely be travelled round within six months.
The kingdom of Pegu was most miserably laid waste.

units.la: A.C.1600. De hâc miserabili calamitate videatur Historia Indiæ Orientalis Petri Iarrigi. Hodie ta-men regnum Pegu ita iterum floret, ut nulla tantæ cladis superfit memo-ria.
units.tr: In the year 1600 of the Christian era. Concerning this wretched calamity, see the History of the East Indies by Pierre Jarric. Today, however, the kingdom of Pegu flourishes again to such an extent that no memory of so great a disaster survives.
The emperor of Java is Magnus Mataran.

units.la: Hic aliquoties urbem Bataviam frustrà obsedit.
units.tr: He several times besieged the city of Batavia in vain.
It came under the power of a single monarch.

units.la: Olim circa A. C. 1300 Zeilonu-ni regi subjecta erat: postea Zingalæ (ita appellantur Zeilonenses) trucidato rege suo Insulam in multa diviserunt regna, donec A. C. 1580 quidam tonsor, cui nomen Maru Raju, totius Insulæ Monarcham se constitueret, sede regiâ in urbe Candy posita.
units.tr: Formerly, around A.C. 1300, it was subject to the king of Zeilon. Afterwards the Zingalæ (this is what the Zeilonese are called) killed their king and divided the island into many kingdoms, until in A.C. 1580 a certain barber named Maru Raju made himself monarch of the whole island, with his royal seat set in the city of Candy.

units.la: Minorum Insularum regna omnia enumerari nequeunt.
units.tr: The kingdoms of all the smaller islands cannot be enumerated.

units.la: Quippe innumeræ; præcipuæ autem Zebut, Molucca, Philippi-na, Borneo, Gilolo, Timor, Banda, Amboyna, Sumatra & Maldivæ. Hæ Maldivæ plus quàm 1100. Insulas amplectuntur, & in XIII Atollas sive provincias dividuntur, quæ omnes unum regem agnoscunt.
units.tr: Indeed they are innumerable; the principal ones, however, are Zebut, Molucca, Philippina, Borneo, Gilolo, Timor, Banda, Amboyna, Sumatra and the Maldives. These Maldives embrace more than 1100 islands and are divided into thirteen Atolls, or provinces, all of which acknowledge one king.
Cataica is either Chinese, or Korean, or Japanese.

units.la: Cataicam vocamus quicquid intra Tartariam & Indiam, Orientem versus, terrarum Insularumq; situm est.
units.tr: We call Cataica whatever lies between Tartary and India, toward the east, both lands and islands.
The kingdom of Sina is said to be the most ancient.

units.la: Ita quidem, ut annales Sinensium ab ipso diluvio continuâ serie reges resq; suas enumerent, quos propediem ex Oriente allatos publicatum iri speramus.
units.tr: Indeed, the annals of the Chinese list their kings and affairs in an unbroken succession from the very deluge itself, which we hope will soon be published, having been brought from the East.

units.la: Supra autem in Antiqua Historia sub Titulo Regni Ægypti diximus Sinenses Ægyptiorum esse coloniam.
units.tr: But above, in the Ancient History, under the title of the Kingdom of Egypt, we said that the Chinese are a colony of the Egyptians.

units.la: Cum Schingvis Khan potentissimum illud Tartarorum imperium condidisset Tartari Sinensibus ab A. C. 1206 per 73. annos continuos bellum intulerunt, usq; ad A.C.1278 quò totam Sinam expugnarunt, & nonaginta annos tenuerunt sub novem regibus, qui Magni Khani Tartarorum dicti sunt.
units.tr: When Genghis Khan had founded that most powerful empire of the Tartars, the Tartars waged war on the Chinese from the year of Christ 1206 for seventy-three continuous years, until in the year of Christ 1278 they conquered all of China, and they held it for ninety years under nine kings, who were called the Great Khans of the Tartars.
Canon. The Chinese expelled the Tartars again.

units.la: A. C. 1368 quidam infimæ conditionis homo Hungyus (Homvu) Tartaros totâ Sinâ pepulit, & illam imperii formam instituit, qvæ ad nostram usque memoriam continuata fuit. Hujus familia dicta fuit Tai-minga, qvam Tartari ante annos aliquot penitus extirparunt, & denuò totam Sinam expugnarunt, ut supra dictum, sub Tit. Regni Tartarici.
units.tr: In the year of Christ 1368, a certain man of the lowest rank, Hungyus (Homvu), drove the Tartars out of all China, and established that form of empire which was continued down to our own memory. His dynasty was called Tai-minga, which the Tartars completely wiped out some years ago, and again conquered all China, as said above, under the title "The Tartar Kingdom."

units.la: Canon.Corea inter Sinenses, Tartaros & Japonios fluctuat.
units.tr: Canon. Corea fluctuates between the Chinese, the Tartars and the Japanese.

units.la: Corea est peninsula inter Sinam & Japoniam peculiari regi subjecta, Hoc regnum crebris vicinorum Tartarorum, Sinensium & Japoniorum bellis petitur.
units.tr: Corea is a peninsula between China and Japan, subject to its own king. This kingdom is often attacked in the wars of its neighbours, the Tartars, the Chinese and the Japanese.

units.la: Insula Japoniæ sive Nippan (ver-naculo idiomate Hippon) divisa LIII regna. Unum olim Mona-cham habuit, quem Dairum appel-labant.
units.tr: The island of Japan, or Nippan (in the vernacular, Hippon), is divided into 53 kingdoms. It once had one monarch, whom they called the Dairi.
The Dairi was succeeded by the Emperors.

units.la: Seculò post Christum Natum de-cimô Sextô, magnis bellicis motibus & cruentis seditionibus sedatis. Cir-ca initium decimi septimi, vel paulò postea, Taicosamma totius Japo-ponie[?] poniæ Imperator à Dairo, sponte se abdicante, declaratus novam Monarchiam condidit. De cujus factis, potentia & magnificentia stupenda plane & incredibilia referuntur. Ei ad nostra usq; tempora successerunt Fideryfamma Ongoschio & Chiongon.
units.tr: In the sixteenth century after the birth of Christ, great wars and bloody uprisings were quelled. Around the beginning of the seventeenth century, or a little later, Taicosamma, Emperor of all Japan, was declared by the Dairi, who voluntarily abdicated, and he founded a new monarchy. Accounts of his deeds, his power and his magnificence are truly astonishing and incredible. His successors down to our own times were Fideryfamma Ongoschio & Chiongon.

units.la: Americani ex nostro orbe originem trahunt.
units.tr: The Americans trace their origin from our world.

units.la: Certum est, jam antiquissimis tem-poribus Orbem illū Occidentalem à Phœnicibus, Carthaginiensibus, Hispa-nis aliisq; nationibus frequentatum habitatumque fuisse. Deinde omnis ipsius notitia periit, cùm excisâ à RoRomanis Chartagine navigationes in Atlantico mari negligerentur.
units.tr: It is certain that already in the most ancient times that Western world was frequented and inhabited by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Spaniards and other nations. Then all knowledge of it perished, when Carthage was destroyed by the Romans and voyages on the Atlantic Sea were neglected.

units.la: Factum fuisse ante multa jam Secula maximam Scytharum per Se-ptentrionem, aliasq; vias, quà terrâ, quà mari, quà glacie in Americam transmigrationem, & eorum multi-tudine universum illum Orbem im-pletum, multis argumentis ostendi potest.
units.tr: That many ages ago there was a very great migration of the Scythians into America, by way of the North and other routes, by land, by sea and over the ice, and that by their multitude that whole world was filled, can be shown by many arguments.

units.la: Singuli propè pagi linguis ac Du-cibus distincti fuerunt, quos Saga-mos seu Casiquas appellarunt, de quorum antiquis rebus nihil omni-nò constat.
units.tr: Nearly every village was distinguished by its language and its leaders, whom they called Sagamos or Casiquas; of their ancient affairs nothing at all is known.
The islands Aiti, Cuba, Jamaica and Borriquen had more famous kingdoms.

units.la: Insula Aiti V regna complecte-batur: sed pauca nobis de illorum rebus innotuêre, nisi ea, quae circa adventum Hispanorum in regiones eas acciderunt.
units.tr: The island Aiti embraced five kingdoms, but few things about their affairs have become known to us, except those that took place around the arrival of the Spaniards in those regions.

units.la: In Septentrione Imperium Mexicanum, ad Meridiem Cu-sconicum[?] omnium amplissima & cultissima fuerunt.
units.tr: In the North the Mexican empire, and in the South the Cusconic [empire], were the most extensive and most civilised.

units.la: Mexicanorum origo deducitur à Navatlacis, qui fuerunt populus Americae Septentrionalis, supra reli-quorum barbariem excultus. Hi NaNavatlaci circa A. C. 820 ex septentrione versus Austrum in VII divisi gentes, totque deniq; castra & Duces migrare coeperunt, donec post diuturnam in itinere moram ad Lacum amoenissimum pervenirent, cujus ripas structis urbibus occupaverunt. Ultimi omnium advenerunt Mexicani, ita à Duce suo Mexio appellati, qui urbem Tenoxtitlam, quæ etiam Mexico dicitur, circa A. C. 1325 in ipso Lacu extruxerunt. Primus ipsorum Rex fuit Tenuch, cui A. C. 1375 successit Acamapixtli, quem Acosta falso primum fuisse regem statuit. Initio exiguæ eorum vires, ac tributum vicinis nationibus pendebant, donec quintus Regum Ifcoatl A. C. 1437 armis pro libertate sumtis imperium amplificaret, vicinis domitis. Hoc brevi tempore adeo crevit, ut sub Motesuma I ab uno Mari ad alterum latissimo ambitu extenderetur. Ultimus regum fuit Motesuma II; cucujus tempore A. C. 1519 Ferdinan-dus Cortesius cum Hispanis regnum Mexicanum detexit, ac intra bien-nium innumerabili multitudine Bar-barorum occisâ universum Carolo V subjecit. Urbs Mexico ex Lacu in Ripam translata ante aliquot annos inundatione & terræ motu tota pe-riisse dicitur.
units.tr: The origin of the Mexicans is traced to the Navatlaci, who were a people of North America, raised above the barbarism of the rest. These Navatlaci, about the year 820 after Christ, divided into seven tribes and began to migrate from the north toward the south, with so many tribes and leaders; until, after a long delay on the journey, they reached a most pleasant lake, the shores of which they occupied with built cities. The Mexicans, named after their leader Mexio, arrived last of all, and about the year 1325 built the city Tenoxtitla, which is also called Mexico, in the lake itself. Their first king was Tenuch, and in 1375 he was succeeded by Acamapixtli, whom Acosta falsely held to have been the first king. At first their strength was small, and they paid tribute to the neighbouring nations, until the fifth of the kings, Ifcoatl, in 1437, took up arms for liberty and enlarged the empire, the neighbouring peoples having been subdued.
