In a short time it grew so much that under Motesuma I it extended over a very wide compass from one sea to the other. The last of the kings was Motesuma II; in whose time, in 1519, Ferdinand Cortes with the Spaniards discovered the Mexican kingdom, and within two years, after an innumerable multitude of barbarians had been slain, subjected the whole to Charles V. The city of Mexico, moved from the lake to the shore, is said to have been wholly destroyed some years ago by a flood and an earthquake.

units.la: In America Meridionali amplis-simum fuit regnū Cusconicum, quod incolæ vocabant Tahuantisuyo, Hi-spani autem Peruviam. Conditores ejus fuerunt Inga, quæ familia, creatô rege Mangocastâ, urbem Cusco circa A. C. 1200 construxit. Hæc ma-gnificentiâ & opibus plerasq; orbis terrarum superavit.
units.tr: In South America the most extensive kingdom was the Cusconic, which the inhabitants called Tahuantisuyo, but the Spaniards Peru. Its founders were the Inga, a family which, after appointing Mangocasta as king, built the city of Cusco about the year 1200 after Christ. This [family] surpassed most of the nations of the world in magnificence and resources.

units.la: A. C. 1500 regnavit Guainacapa, qui regnô Quitonico subjugato universum imperium admirandis stru-ctu[?]turis exornavit. Obiit A. C. 1523[?], duobus relictis filiis, inter quos ita divisit imperium, ut major natu, nomine Guascar, regnum Casconicum haberet; Attahu-Alpa vero, quem corrupte Attabalibam vocant, regno Quitonis praesset. Sed cum in illa divisione incertum mansisset cuinam fratrum provincia Tho-mebamba cedere deberet, magnum pro ea inter ipsos dissidium exortum Hispanis occasionem praebuit Peruviae invadendae, quam recens detexerat Franciscus Pizarrus. Interea Attahu-Alpa fratre Guascare capto & interfecto solus imperio potitus fuit. Hujus ingentes copias facili negotio Pizantus[?] fudit, ipsumque captum, quanquam incredibilem auri & argenti vim promitteret, nefarie stran-gulavit. Ita A. C. 1533 imperium Ingarum sive Cusconicum titulô Peruviae ad Hispanos pervenit. Nam Qui post Attahu-Alpam regnarunt InIngares , nempe Paulo & Mango , non nisi montanas quasdam provincias, latronum potius quàm regum more, obtinuerunt. Ultimus omnium Ingarum regum fuit Xaires Topa Jnca, qui A. C. 1557 sese Philippo II Hispaniarum regi subjecit.
units.tr: In the year 1500 Guainacapa reigned, who, after subjugating the kingdom of Quito, adorned the whole empire with admirable structures. He died in 1523 [?], leaving two sons, between whom he so divided the empire that the elder, named Guascar, should have the Cusconic kingdom; but Attahu-Alpa, whom they corruptly call Attabalibas, should preside over the kingdom of Quito. But since in that division it remained uncertain to which of the brothers the province of Thomebamba should belong, a great dissension arose between them over it, which gave the Spaniards an occasion for invading Peru, which Francis Pizarro had lately discovered. Meanwhile Attahu-Alpa, his brother Guascar having been captured and killed, alone gained possession of the empire. Pizarro easily routed his huge forces, and when he had taken him captive, though he promised an incredible quantity of gold and silver, he treacherously strangled him. Thus in 1533 the empire of the Incas, or the Cusconic [empire], under the title of Peru, passed to the Spaniards. For the Incas who reigned after Attahu-Alpa, namely Paulo and Mango, held only certain mountain provinces, more in the manner of robbers than of kings. The last of all the Inca kings was Xaires Topa Inca, who in 1557 submitted himself to Philip II, king of the Spains.

units.la: Hi Peruvianis ad Austrum vicini nullum Regem, sed Duces tantum suos agnoscunt, & incredibili fortitudine hactenus soli omnium ferè Americanorum contra Hispanos libertatem suam defenderunt: ita quidem, ut Societas Indiae Occidentalis spem conceperit auxilio Chilensium universâ Peruviâ & auriferis montibus Hispanos pellisposfe. [?] In quem finem missus A. C.1644 Navarchus Brouverus, qui fœdus cum illis contra Hispanos iniret. Sed spes tùm temporis irrita facta fuit.
units.tr: These neighbours of the Peruvians to the south acknowledge no king, but only their own leaders, and with incredible bravery have so far defended their liberty against the Spaniards, almost alone of all the Americans. So much so that the Dutch West India Company conceived the hope that, with the help of the Chileans, the Spaniards could be driven from the whole of Peru and its gold-bearing mountains. To this end Admiral Brouwer was sent in 1644, to make an alliance with them against the Spaniards. But the hope was then frustrated.
The Brazilians live without law and without king.

units.la: Nulla Reipublicæ species apud Brasilianos reperitur, sed domesticum tantùm imperium agnoscunt. Qui seniores natu, & plures interfecerunt hostes, quandam veluti Ducum autoritatem apud eos obtinent. Ipsorum igitur, ut & aliorum Barbarorum historia, nihil memoratu dignum habet: mera enim inter se latrocinia gerunt.
units.tr: No form of commonwealth is found among the Brazilians; they acknowledge only domestic authority. Those who are older by birth and have killed more enemies hold a certain authority among them, as it were, of leaders. Therefore their history, like that of other barbarians, has nothing worth recording: for they carry on nothing but mutual robberies.
The English discovered the kingdom of New Albion.

units.la: A. C. 1580 Franciscus Draco Anglus regnum quoddam Barbarum detexit, quod Novam Albionem vocavit sed ab eo tempore nihil de eo certi cognitum fuit.
units.tr: In the year 1580, Francis Drake, an Englishman, discovered a certain barbarous kingdom, which he called New Albion, but from that time nothing certain has been known about it.
The Southern Land has not yet been discovered.

units.la: Restat adhuc ingens Orbis pars versus Meridiem, cujus litora quidem & ignes procul à navigantibus conspiciuntur, ingredi autem, nisi interdum aquandi ergo, propter incolarum ferociam, non audent Quidam Hispanus nomine Petrus Ferdinandus del Quier, A. C. 1617 Regi Hispaniae accuratam, ut jactabat, earum terrarum descriptionem exhibuit, ibiq; immensam auri argentique vim, incolasq; factionibus inter sese ac odiis divisas, facile armis Eu-ropæis superari posse, narravit. Non semel quoq; Societas Indiæ Orientalis de expeditione in Orbem illum incognitum deliberavit suscipienda: Sed hactenus res intra voluntatem ac conatum stetit.
units.tr: There remains still a vast part of the globe towards the south, whose shores and fires are indeed seen from afar by navigators, but which they do not dare to enter, except occasionally for the sake of watering, because of the fierceness of the inhabitants. A certain Spaniard named Petrus Ferdinandus del Quier, in the year 1617, presented to the King of Spain an accurate, as he boasted, description of those lands, and he related that an immense quantity of gold and silver was there, and that the inhabitants, divided among themselves by factions and hatreds, could easily be overcome by European arms. More than once also the East India Company has deliberated about undertaking an expedition into that unknown world; but so far the matter has remained at the level of wish and attempt.
